candidates.evidence: Three significant peaks at 155.7, 299.6 and 354.1 cm-1 (fitted, measured). I have no offline reference library and did not verify any literature mode table, so no formula can be matched with confidence. The strongest feature is a dominant ~156 cm-1 mode with a second strong mode near 354 cm-1; this pattern needs a reference spectrum to test.

hint_reasoning: The task is 'identify' and material_hint is null, so there is no stated material to check against. I did not use the directory name as evidence. The identification rests only on the peak positions, widths and relative intensities in spectrum.csv, and those do not match any material I can confirm.

properties.name: identification
properties.source: No peak set matched to a reference I can verify offline

limits: I cannot identify the material with confidence. The three significant peaks (155.7, 299.6, 354.1 cm-1) would need to be compared against a reference Raman library or literature mode table for layered candidates. None was available offline and I did not cite any literature values.

Above about 420 cm-1 no feature reaches 3 sigma. The noise is about 240 counts and the features are about 400-600 counts, so the weak bands at 478-1071 cm-1 that a naive peak search lists are consistent with noise plus background and are not reported as peaks.

The broad background (fluorescence-like slope) and the choice of baseline change the amplitudes and widths of the weak peaks. The 299.6 cm-1 width and the 382.4 cm-1 feature are the least reliable numbers.

No Si substrate line is claimed. There is only a weak feature at 524.4 cm-1 (t≈2.3), 3.7 cm-1 from the Si 520.7 cm-1 line, which is too weak to call. No calibration standard was given, so absolute shifts may carry an offset of roughly 1-2 cm-1.
The spectrum starts at 60 cm-1. Features at 70-190 cm-1 other than the 155.7 cm-1 peak are not significant (t≈2-3).
This is one unpolarized backscattering spectrum. No polarization dependence was measured, so no symmetry (irrep) or polarization pattern can be assigned to any peak.
Layer number, defect level and strain cannot be determined from these data.
The single-point spike at 897.47 cm-1 (9238 counts against neighbours of about 1500-1700) was replaced by the neighbour average before fitting. No other spikes were found at the 4.5-sigma level.
